moong_chilla_curd.description: High-protein savoury pancakes of yellow moong dal with green chutney and curd. No onion, garlic or root vegetables, so it suits Jain kitchens.
ingredients: ½ cup yellow moong dal, soaked 4 hours and drained
steps: Grind the soaked dal with green chilli, hing, cumin and a little water into a thick, pourable batter.
Stir in coriander and salt.
Heat a non-stick tawa on medium heat and smear with a few drops of oil.
Pour a ladle of batter and spread it into a thin circle.
Cook 2-3 minutes until the edges lift and the base is golden, then flip and cook 1 minute.
Blend the chutney ingredients with a splash of water until smooth.
Serve 2 chillas hot with chutney and curd.
moong_chilla_curd.tips: Crumble 2 tbsp paneer into the batter for roughly 4 g more protein.

paneer_paratha_curd.description: Stuffed whole wheat flatbread with spiced crumbled paneer — rich in protein and very filling.
steps: Knead wheat flour, salt and water into a soft dough. Rest 10 min.
Mix crumbled paneer with all spices and coriander. Set aside.
Divide dough into 2 balls. Roll each into a small circle.
Place 2–3 tbsp filling in centre, fold edges over and seal.
Gently roll again into a flat paratha (~6 inch).
Cook on a hot tawa with a little ghee/oil, flipping twice until golden.
Serve with cold curd and pickle.
paneer_paratha_curd.tips: Press the stuffed paratha gently with a spatula while cooking for even heat distribution.

besan_cheela_chutney.description: Quick chickpea-flour pancakes — one of the fastest high-protein breakfasts you can make.
steps: Whisk besan, water, turmeric, ajwain, and salt into a smooth lump-free batter.
Fold in chopped onion, chilli, and coriander.
Heat a tawa, grease lightly, pour batter and spread thin.
Cook 2–3 min until bubbles form, flip and cook 1 min.
Blend all chutney ingredients until smooth.
Serve 2 cheelas with green chutney.
besan_cheela_chutney.tips: Add 2 tbsp curd to the batter for softer, fluffier cheelas.

dal_tadka_thali.description: Everyday North Indian thali: toor dal with a cumin-garlic tadka, rotis, a dry mixed vegetable sabzi and salad.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin seeds, pinch of hing, 1 dry red chilli
1 tsp ghee or oil for the tadka
2 cups mixed vegetables (beans, carrot, peas, cauliflower)
½ tsp each: cumin, turmeric, coriander powder
1 cup whole wheat atta, water, pinch of salt
steps: Pressure-cook the dal with turmeric and 2 cups water for 3-4 whistles. Whisk until smooth.
For the sabzi, heat oil, add cumin, then the vegetables and spices. Cover and cook 10-12 minutes until tender.
Knead atta with water and salt into a soft dough. Rest 10 minutes, then roll and cook rotis on a hot tawa.
For the tadka, heat ghee, add cumin, hing, red chilli, garlic and ginger, then onion and tomato. Cook 4-5 minutes.
Pour the tadka into the dal and simmer 3 minutes.
Serve dal, 2 rotis, sabzi and salad per plate.
dal_tadka_thali.tips: A squeeze of lemon on the dal helps your body absorb its iron.

rajma_chawal.description: North India's favourite comfort food — kidney beans over rice with cooling raita. High protein, high fibre.
ingredients: 1 cup basmati or rice (white or brown)
steps: Pressure cook soaked rajma with salt and water (6–7 whistles) until soft.
Cook rice separately.
Heat oil in a kadhai. Add cumin, then onion purée — cook 10 min until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 2 min. Add tomato purée + all spices, cook 10 min.
Add cooked rajma with some cooking water. Simmer 10 min until thick.
Whisk curd with grated cucumber, cumin powder and salt for raita.
Serve rajma over rice with raita on the side.
rajma_chawal.tips: Use an Instant Pot to skip overnight soaking — pressure cook dry rajma for 45 min.

palak_paneer_roti.description: Classic spinach-paneer curry — iron from spinach + protein from paneer = one of the most nutritious vegetarian curries.
ingredients: ½ cup any dal (cooked, for the side)
steps: Blanch spinach in boiling water 2 min, then transfer to ice water. Blend smooth.
Fry paneer cubes lightly in 1 tsp oil until golden. Set aside.
In same pan, heat oil. Add cumin, then diced onion — sauté 8 min.
Add ginger-garlic paste + tomatoes, cook 8 min until oil separates.
Add spinach purée + all spices, mix well and simmer 5 min.
Add paneer, fold in gently. Simmer 3 min. Stir in cream if using.
Serve with warm rotis and a small bowl of dal.
palak_paneer_roti.tips: Blanching and ice-bathing spinach keeps the gravy bright green and preserves nutrients.

khichdi_curd.description: India's original one-pot comfort food — easily digestible, balanced macros, and very soothing.
steps: Wash and soak rice + moong dal together 20 min.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker. Add bay leaf, cloves, cumin — let splutter.
Add ginger, sauté 1 min. Add vegetables, turmeric and salt.
Add drained rice + dal, mix well. Add 3.5 cups water.
Pressure cook 3 whistles on medium heat.
Let pressure release naturally. Adjust consistency with hot water.
Serve with cold curd.
khichdi_curd.tips: Add 1 tbsp lemon juice after cooking for a flavour boost without extra calories.

paneer_bhurji_roti.description: Scrambled spiced paneer — the vegetarian answer to scrambled eggs. Fast, high protein, very satisfying.
steps: Heat oil, add cumin. Once it splutters, add onion and sauté 5 min.
Add capsicum, cook 2 min. Add tomatoes + all spices, cook until soft.
Crumble in paneer, fold gently. Cook 3–4 min — don't over-mix.
Garnish with coriander. Serve with warm rotis and a simple cucumber-tomato salad.
paneer_bhurji_roti.tips: Soak packaged paneer in warm water 10 min before using to make it softer.

chole_brown_rice.description: Spiced chickpea curry — one of the best plant-based protein sources with complex flavour from whole spices.
steps: Pressure cook soaked chana with salt and water — 5 whistles.
Cook brown rice separately.
Heat oil, add cumin. Add onions, fry 10 min until deep golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, fry 2 min. Add tomato purée + all spices.
Cook masala 10 min until oil separates.
Add cooked chana + some cooking water. Simmer 10–12 min.
Garnish with coriander and a squeeze of lemon. Serve with brown rice.
chole_brown_rice.tips: Amchur (dry mango powder) gives that signature tangy punch — don't skip it.

oats_pb.description: Simple, fast and highly effective — complex carbs + banana sugar + peanut butter protein for sustained energy.
steps: Add oats and milk to a saucepan. Cook on medium heat 3–4 min, stirring.
Pour into a bowl. Top with sliced banana.
Add peanut butter on top — it melts slightly from the heat.
Drizzle jaggery and sprinkle cinnamon.
oats_pb.tips: Overnight version: soak oats in milk overnight in the fridge. Add toppings in the morning — zero cooking required.

sprouts_chaat_snack.description: No-cook high-protein snack — sprouted moong are nutritionally superior to cooked, with extra vitamin C.
steps: If using raw sprouts, microwave or steam 2 min for safety.
Mix all chopped vegetables with sprouts.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala and salt.
Toss well and garnish with coriander.
sprouts_chaat_snack.tips: Grow your own sprouts: soak moong dal overnight, drain, keep in a wet cloth 24–36 hrs. Free protein!

yogurt_almonds.description: Effortless high-protein snack — Greek yogurt has nearly 2x the protein of regular curd.
steps: Spoon Greek yogurt into a bowl.
Drizzle jaggery on top.
Add chopped nuts and a pinch of cinnamon.
Eat immediately or refrigerate up to 2 hours.
yogurt_almonds.tips: Make your own Greek yogurt: hang regular curd in a muslin cloth 2–3 hours to drain whey. Same protein, half the cost.

chana_chai.description: The simplest high-protein Indian snack — roasted Bengal gram is one of the best protein-per-rupee foods.
steps: The chana needs no cooking — pour into a bowl and add chaat masala.
For chai: boil water with ginger and crushed cardamom.
Add tea leaves, boil 1 min. Add milk and sugar, boil 2 more min.
Strain and serve alongside the chana.
chana_chai.tips: 50g roasted chana = 10–11g protein for under ₹10. Best value protein snack in India.

idli_sambar.description: South India's iconic breakfast — fermented batter idlis with lentil sambar. Light yet nutritious.
ingredients: 2 cups idli rice + 1 cup urad dal (soaked and blended, fermented 8–12 hrs)
steps: Blend soaked urad dal smooth. Mix with ground rice batter. Add salt and ferment 8–12 hrs.
Pour batter into greased idli moulds, steam 10–12 min.
For sambar: pressure cook toor dal. Prepare tadka of mustard, curry leaves, tomato + sambar powder. Mix with dal + tamarind. Simmer 8 min.
Blend coconut, chilli, chana dal and salt with water for chutney.
Serve 3 idlis with sambar and chutney.
idli_sambar.tips: Use instant idli mix if fermentation feels like too much effort — still a healthy breakfast!

quinoa_chole_bowl.description: Quinoa topped with chole cooked without onion or garlic, and a crunchy cucumber-tomato salad.
ingredients: 1 cup cooked kabuli chana (soaked overnight, pressure-cooked)
½ tsp each: chana masala, coriander powder, red chilli powder
Lemon juice, salt and chaat masala
steps: Cook the quinoa in ⅔ cup water for about 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Heat oil, add cumin and hing, then the tomato puree and spices. Cook until the oil separates.
Add the chana and ½ cup water. Simmer 8-10 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken.
Toss cucumber and tomato with lemon, salt and chaat masala.
Spoon quinoa into a bowl, top with chole and salad.
quinoa_chole_bowl.tips: Rinse quinoa thoroughly before cooking to remove its bitter coating.

tofu_quinoa.description: High-protein tofu with nutty quinoa and stir-fried vegetables — fast, colourful, and filling.
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (capsicum, broccoli, peas, carrot)
Spring onions + sesame seeds to garnish
steps: Press tofu between paper towels 10 min to remove moisture. Cut into cubes.
Cook quinoa in 1 cup water, 15 min.
Heat oil in a wok on high heat. Add tofu and fry until golden on all sides.
Push tofu aside. Add ginger-garlic, then vegetables. Stir-fry 3–4 min on high.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil. Toss everything together.
Serve over quinoa, garnish with spring onions and sesame.
tofu_quinoa.tips: For crispier tofu: dust with cornflour before frying, or bake at 200°C for 20 min.
